chunks: From him, from Hammad, from Ibrahim ibn Umar, from Abu Ayyub, who said: Abu al-Subbah, the freedman of Bassam al-Sayrafi, narrated to me, saying:

I intended to enter into Ihram for Tamattu' (the Hajj of Tamattu'), so I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'How should I say?' He said, 'You should say: O Allah, I intend to perform the Tamattu' of Umrah until Hajj, according to Your Book and the Sunnah of Your Prophet. And if you wish, you may keep silent (intend) what you desire.'

key_terms.أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ع: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) (Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq)
key_terms.الإِحْرَام: Ihram (ritual state of consecration for pilgrimage)
key_terms.التَّمَتُّع: Al-Tamattu' (the act of enjoying/performing Umrah until Hajj)
key_terms.بِالْمُتْعَةِ: Al-Mut'ah (Tamattu', a type of Hajj combining Umrah and Hajj)

ai.seo_question: What is the correct supplication to recite when entering Ihram for Hajj al-Tamattu'?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfahani's al-Isfihar clarifies the specific verbal declaration required for the Hajj of Tamattu', emphasizing the dual intention of Umrah and subsequent Hajj while remaining flexible with silent intent. It highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on grounding ritual acts in both the Quranic text and the Prophet's Sunnah, ensuring the validity of the pilgrimage through precise adherence to the Imam's guidance.
